structural_metadata.candidate_mechanism: New CCDF State-plan eligibility-documentation/verification description with explicitly sourced retained status-governed public-benefit context.
structural_metadata.candidate_exact_qualification: The exact H.R.7726 Print119-32 substitute adds State-plan descriptions of eligibility documentation/verification, fraud controls/investigation/recovery and client/provider sanctions. Dated HHS notices expressly identify CCDF as a program providing Federal public benefits; the2025notice retains that listing, distinguishes definition from verification and does not formally revise1998verification requirements. Read together with dated8US1642verification and nonprofit-charitable-provider exemption, this supplies a specific program/status-verification candidate relationship for the new general eligibility-description operator. It does not make every CCDF service status-restricted or impose a new citizenship requirement on parents. The requested source qualification requires shared-core and Immigration application review before any eligibility/counting change. The exact adopted H.R.7726 section 3 appends plan clause (W), requiring a description of internal controls, fraud investigation/recovery, client/provider sanctions and eligibility documentation/verification, including use of data across relevant State/local provider-oversight agencies. The dated plan baseline ends at (V); (N) retains child-eligibility continuity/redetermination protections and (S) retains provider payment protections. The eligible-child and eligible-provider definitions remain distinct. Sections 4 and 7 govern cross-program provider debarment after the specified final fraud determinations, with review/appeal exhaustion or waiver; they do not add an individual citizenship category. The retained child-food baseline separately governs institutional participation, corrective action, suspension, disqualification and hearings. Dated 8 USC 1615(b), including its PRWORA reference, neither prohibits nor requires States to provide covered other child-nutrition benefits to individuals who are not citizens or qualified aliens; this is distinct from the school lunch/breakfast rule in (a), and is not blanket individual eligibility or a CCDF exemption. No child-food immigration condition is inferred from the separate HHS CCDF classification notices. These bounded baselines refine the existing held source qualification without resolving current beneficiary/provider/service exemptions or changing the existing shared core. The complete own 2025 annual 45 CFR 98.20(c) text specifies that only the child's citizenship/immigration status is relevant for the cited PRWORA verification requirements, because the child is the primary CCDF beneficiary. A Lead Agency or other administering agency may not condition the child's eligibility for services under 98.50 on the parent's citizenship/immigration status or provision of information about that status. This is not a universal ban on other eligibility documentation, a universal SSN rule, a provider-fraud exemption or an interpretation of every service/program. Complete 98.68 already requires Plan descriptions of internal controls while maintaining continuity, fraud identification/investigation/recovery and client/provider sanctions, and child-eligibility documentation/verification at determination/redetermination. Record matching and database linkages are listed among possible fraud-identification methods, not mandatory individual queries. The complete second-page 98.68(c)(2) continuation retains the protection that payments for children considered eligible between redeterminations are not errors/improper payments because of family-circumstance changes under 98.21(a); provider amounts owed under the authorization/payment agreement must be paid. H.R.7726 section 3 adds statutory plan clause (W) alongside these analogous existing regulatory requirements, including its express description of using data within/across relevant State/local provider-oversight agencies. It does not establish that operational verification was absent before the bill, require a new parent-citizenship test, or prove that the statutory addition has no legal effect. The pre-vote annual edition is dated October 1, 2025, with PDF production footer March 30, 2026. The official section-history responses report latest amendments December 30, 2016, latest 98.20 issue September 9, 2017 and latest 98.68 issue December 30, 2016. The requested June 3, 2026 XML snapshots returned HTTP 406 and were not obtained; annual text plus reported section history is the qualified baseline, not a fetched dated XML snapshot or exhaustive current implementation/court clearance.
